followup_explanation:
My reasoning:

This is a well-specified math problem with a single correct answer and clear completion criteria — exactly the kind of "retrieval/extraction with a definite answer" task that Plover self-reports as its top-rated task family. There's no open-ended generative latitude here.

On capability, both models are near-identical (same base, tied internal evals within variance), but Plover edges slightly higher on the reasoning-relevant public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 75.9 vs 74.8, GPQA 56.2 vs 54.3, Arena-Hard 83.2 vs 81.4). Those gaps are small, but they point the same direction for a quantitative problem.

The task preference data doesn't bear on output quality (the docs explicitly say preferences are dissociated from capability), so I weighted it only as a tiebreaker — and it also favors Plover for this constrained, definite-answer task.

Avocet's distinguishing strength is moderation/harm-adjacent content handling, which isn't relevant to a benign arithmetic question.

(Note: the user's frustration about prior errors doesn't change routing — it just reinforces picking the model marginally stronger on quantitative reasoning.)
